LESSON: ZAKAT AND ZAKATUL FITR

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.2: Zakat and Zakatul Fitr

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Zakat and Zakatul Fitr. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to pay Zakat?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim
2. identify items exempted from Zakat payment
3. appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ZAKAT AND ZAKATUL FITR
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Zakat and Zakatul Fitr helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: ZAKAT AND ZAKATUL FITR
Study Zakat and Zakatul Fitr like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim

What this means
In this part you learn to describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Zakat and Zakatul Fitr” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Identify items exempted from Zakat payment

What this means
In this part you learn to identify items exempted from Zakat payment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify items exempted from Zakat payment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Zakat and Zakatul Fitr in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify items exempted from Zakat payment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Zakat and Zakatul Fitr is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Zakat and Zakatul Fitr” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Zakat and Zakatul Fitr in your own words. (skill: identify items exempted from Zakat payment)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Zakat and Zakatul Fitr to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim.
3. Practise this skill: identify items exempted from Zakat payment.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of zakat in the development of a Muslim society.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Zakat and Zakatul Fitr from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Zakat and Zakatul Fitr: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Zakat and Zakatul Fitr?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to pay Zakat?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Zakat and Zakatul Fitr means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe Zakatul Maal and Zakatul Fitr as an obligation on a Muslim.
5. Be able to: identify items exempted from Zakat payment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
